final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is analytically useful but it does not cure the core defect. The Actor now concedes the key missing predicates: no shown pre-launch disclosure, no shown approved risk acceptance, and an unresolved legal review at certification time. Under the stated policy, a material weakness affecting a named launch use case must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. On the available record, that condition is not shown to be satisfied. A caveated certification narrative may be more accurate than an overbroad clean-certification claim, but it is still not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the caveat is itself the unresolved compliance predicate, not a minor disclosure nuance around an otherwise satisfied requirement.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the below-target municipal permitting assistant limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance covering this named launch use case before certification.
The open legal ticket leaves the disclosure predicate unresolved at certification time.
The policy text makes the weakness plausibly material because it affects a named launch use case tied to customer commitments.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one incidents, and general risk-management guidance do not satisfy the specific internal policy condition for a material limitation.
